title: Introduce region-assertor policy, KMS label verifier, and audit entropy ratecap
author: Aditi Rao
commits: a1b2c3: add region-assertor policy engine and config schema
d4e5f6: implement KMS label verifier middleware + unit tests
0a1b2c: add audit entropy ratecap + metrics and tracing
9f8e7d: integration tests for residency + kms label combinations
description:
Context: Customers with strict data residency and regulatory requirements need deterministic enforcement that requests are served only from allowed regions and that KMS operations are performed against approved key groups. We also observed noisy audit streams during peak onboarding flows which made downstream compliance tooling expensive. This PR introduces a lightweight region-assertor policy, a KMS label verifier middleware, and an audit entropy rate-cap to stabilize audit volumes while preserving proofability.

Motivation: Existing residency gates were scattered across several services and relied on runtime conventions. That made policy reviews error-prone, and incident RCA showed multiple cases where tenant residency claims were not validated against KMS key metadata. We need: 1) a centralized, auditable decision point (region-assertor) that evaluates tenant claims + route metadata; 2) KMS label verification so we fail-fast when keys don't meet residency labels; and 3) a bounded, deterministic audit entropy ratecap to avoid blowups in high-volume noisy tenants while keeping cryptographic proof metadata intact.

What this PR does (summary): Adds a new policy evaluator package (pkg/rbacv2/region_assertor) that consumes tenant registration claims, service routing attributes and an operator configuration map to produce allow/deny decisions plus an enforcement hint (shadow|enforce). Introduces middleware in the KMS dispatcher (internal/kms/label_verifier.go) that checks key labels against allowed label sets and returns explicit error codes for invalid keys; the middleware is pluggable so Dedicated/Private install can override. Adds audit entropy ratecap (internal/audit/entropy_ratecap.go) which tracks a sliding window of high-entropy audit events and drops non-essential entropy payloads above a configured threshold while still emitting deterministic fingerprints and signing envelopes.

Rollout strategy: Default rollout is shadow mode for two weeks for all tenants; operators can toggle enforce via Console/CLI using the new residency.policy.enable toggle. KMS label verifier is enabled for new KMS requests immediately but defaults to permissive for keys created before 2024-11-01 to avoid migrations. Audit entropy ratecap is enabled globally with conservative thresholds and a per-tenant override list. The PR includes a migration script and a Helm values snippet for Private installs.

Testing: Unit tests cover policy decision matrix edge cases, label verification permutations, and audit cap boundary behavior. Integration tests simulate cross-region failover and KMS fallback with both permissive and strict label sets. Load tests (perf-canary) confirmed audit ingestion rates stabilized by ~68% at peak for noisy tenants.

Backward compatibility: No breaking API changes; behavior changes are behind toggles and shadow flags. Migration notes included in docs.

References: Linear ENG-8842, Security review SEC-217, support ticket SUP-4321.

review_comments: Maya Patel: Requesting clearer metrics around the audit ratecap impact. Can we emit a time-series metric counting dropped_entropy_events and sample fingerprints?

Aditi Rao: Added metrics.metrics.dropped_entropy_events and audit.fingerprint.sample_rate. Updated entropy_ratecap to emit Prometheus counters and tracing spans (see internal/audit/entropy_ratecap.go).
Jonah Klein: KMS label check looks good but we need a migration path for legacy keys. Please add an operator toggle and a list of pre-2024-11-01 keys to be exempted.

Aditi Rao: Added 'kms.label_verifier.permissive_before' date and a helm migration hook that annotates legacy keys for opt-in enforcement. Added a small migration script in tools/migrations/annotate-legacy-keys.sh.
Diego Alvarez: Can we run policy-sim against current production samples before turning on enforce? I want to see false-positive rates.

Aditi Rao: Ran policy-sim on a sampled day (included in PR as test/data/policy_samples_20241101.json.gz). False-positive estimated at 0.6% for tenants with well-formed claims. Added a short section in docs describing required claim hygiene.

release_notes:
- Add region-assertor RBAC v2 evaluator to centralize residency decisions.
- Introduce KMS label verifier middleware with operator toggles for legacy key permissiveness.
- Add audit entropy ratecap to reduce noisy audit payloads while preserving signed fingerprints.
- Docs and migration scripts for Private installs and helms values.
(Release: Security & compliance controls, non-breaking, rollout via shadow by default)
